plants.name: Tulipa gesneriana
plants.description: Rows of cup-shaped blooms in saturated crimson, butter yellow, blush pink and near-black stripe the Dutch bulb fields like a painter's palette. Around Lisse, millions of tulips open together and turn the flat landscape into ribbons of color.
plants.bloomingSeason: Mid-April to early May in the Netherlands, with the peak around the third week of April
plants.location: Lisse and the bulb-growing region of the Netherlands, Europe
plants.funFact: Tulips were so prized in 17th-century Holland that single bulbs reportedly sold for more than the price of a canal house during 'tulip mania'.

plants.name: Eschscholzia californica
plants.description: This silky, cup-shaped wildflower glows like molten gold across sunny hillsides and grasslands. Its petals close on cloudy days and at night, then open wide in bright sun. They carpet the landscape in orange.
plants.bloomingSeason: Spring, with March through May usually the strongest bloom
plants.location: California, USA, in grasslands, hillsides and native gardens
plants.funFact: California's state flower has finely divided blue-green leaves. Its petals fold shut at night and in cool, overcast weather, which protects the pollen.

plants.name: Wisteria floribunda
plants.description: Long, fragrant chains of pea-like flowers hang from twisting vines and trellises. They create tunnels of lavender and violet that sway in the spring breeze. Japan's famous wisteria parks come alive at this time of year.
plants.bloomingSeason: Mid-April to mid-May in many parts of Japan
plants.location: Japan, including famous wisteria gardens such as Ashikaga Flower Park in Tochigi
plants.funFact: Japanese wisteria twines clockwise, while Chinese wisteria twines counterclockwise. Old vines can live for well over a century and grow into enormous canopies.

plants.name: Camellia sasanqua
plants.description: While the Northern Hemisphere greets spring, Australian gardens are turning to autumn. They are lit by this shrub's delicate, often lightly scented blooms. The flowers have silky petals around a bright boss of golden stamens. They open on glossy evergreen bushes, and gardeners value them as an early start to the camellia season.
plants.bloomingSeason: Autumn, beginning in April and May in Australia and continuing into early winter
plants.location: Gardens across temperate Australia (Southern Hemisphere), native to Japan and China
plants.funFact: Camellia sasanqua is a close relative of the tea plant, Camellia sinensis. Its seeds are pressed to make oil used in cooking and cosmetics in parts of Asia.
